keywords_en: Criminal; Unlawful Detention; First Instance; Basic People's Court; Hainan Province; Natural Person; Criminal Law; Distinction Between Crime of Kidnapping and Crime of Unlawful Detention; Boundary Between Claiming Debts and Extorting Property; Partially Upheld; Illegal Pyramid Schemes; Hostage Taking; Demand for Debt
full_text_en:
Huang Yongzhu — Illegal Detention Case

Procuratorial Authority: Zhendong District People's Procuratorate of Haikou City, Hainan Province.

Defendant: Huang Yongzhu, male, 28 years old, a farmer from Kaijiang County, Sichuan Province, arrested on May 16, 2000, on suspicion of kidnapping.

Defense Counsel: Zhang Xiaodong, lawyer from Hainan Foreign Economic Law Firm.

The case concerning the defendant Huang Yongzhu's alleged kidnapping was initiated by the Zhendong District People's Procuratorate of Haikou City, Hainan Province, which filed a public prosecution with the Zhendong District People's Court of Haikou City.

The indictment alleged: The defendant Huang Yongzhu, acting in concert with Wang Fei, Chen Bo, Huang Jian, Su Rong, Zhang Jun, Tang Bo, Jiang Bo, and others, seized and controlled Zou Hongxing, who was engaged in illegal pyramid scheme activities, and telephoned Zou Hongxing's wife demanding a ransom of RMB 60,000. After receiving the report, the public security officers arrived at the scene and rescued Zou Hongxing. The following day, Huang Yongzhu was apprehended. Huang Yongzhu's conduct violated Article 239, paragraph 1 of the Criminal Law of the PRC, constituting the crime of kidnapping, and he should be punished according to law.

The prosecutorial authority read into the record at trial the victim's family's report materials, the public security organ's certificate regarding the case solving and the arrest of Huang Yongzhu, the victim's statement, the testimony of witnesses Zou Weihong, Li Yunsheng, Jiang Yin'e, and Jiang Yue'e, and produced photographs of the crime scene, photographs of the knife used as a tool and the seizure record, photographs of the victim's injuries, and other evidence.

The defendant Huang Yongzhu had no objection to the facts alleged in the indictment, but argued that he had detained Zou Hongxing in order to demand from Zou Hongxing's wife the return of funds paid for a pyramid scheme, and that this was not kidnapping. Huang Yongzhu's defense counsel submitted that, from both a subjective and objective perspective, Huang Yongzhu's conduct only constituted the crime of illegal detention, that he was an accomplice in the joint crime, and that he had confessed his guilt, warranting a lighter punishment.

The Zhendong District People's Court of Haikou City found upon trial:

On January 31, 2000, after paying RMB 3,900 to his upliner Jiang Yue'e, the defendant Huang Yongzhu joined an illegal pyramid scheme operating under the names "franchise chain" and "network marketing," obtained business agent status, and gathered with other persons who had joined the pyramid scheme in the Baishamen Zhongcun area of Haikou City to receive pyramid scheme training. On the evening of April 2 of the same year, while Huang Yongzhu and other pyramid scheme participants were attending a "Successful People's Sharing Session" lecture, pyramid scheme participants Huang Jian, Wang Fei, and Chen Bo suddenly entered the meeting place, claiming that the pyramid scheme was a fraud and that if anyone wanted to go home, they should go to their upliner to get their money back. At about 8:00 p.m. that evening, Huang Yongzhu, together with Chen Bo, Huang Jian, Wang Fei, Su Rong, Zhang Jun, and Tang Bo (all at large), who were carrying weapons, went to Room 304, Building G, Haijing Garden, Haidian Island, to demand RMB 60,000 from pyramid scheme participant Zou Hongxing (the husband of Jiang Yin'e, who was the cousin of Jiang Yue'e), and took Zou Hongxing away from Haijing Garden. Zou Hongxing asked his friend Li Yunsheng to follow. On the grass outside the wall of Haijing Garden, Zou Hongxing was forced to telephone his wife Jiang Yin'e, demanding that she immediately raise RMB 60,000 in cash to ransom him. Subsequently, Huang Yongzhu, Chen Bo, and five others escorted Zou Hongxing and Li Yunsheng in the direction of Beiguocheng. During the journey, Zhang Jun left, and another pyramid scheme participant, Jiang Bo (at large), arrived and joined in seizing Zou Hongxing. As the group walked, they negotiated the location for handing over the money with Jiang Yin'e by telephone, agreeing to exchange the money for the person on the grass at the northernmost end of Heping Avenue. Huang Yongzhu, Chen Bo, and five others escorted Zou Hongxing and Li Yunsheng to the agreed location, and sent Li Yunsheng to find Jiang Yin'e to collect the money. Li did not return. While they were guarding Zou Hongxing and continuing to negotiate with Jiang Yin'e by mobile phone, they saw public security officers arriving and fled in all directions. The victim Zou Hongxing also took the opportunity to run away, and in the darkness, his back was slashed with a cleaver, causing minor injuries. After rescuing Zou Hongxing, the public security officers arrested Huang Yongzhu the next day at his rented residence.

It was also found that the defendant Huang Yongzhu and the at-large Chen Bo, Huang Jian, Wang Fei, Su Rong, Tang Bo, Jiang Bo, and others were all downline members developed by Jiang Yue'e in the illegal pyramid scheme. Jiang Yue'e's upliner was her cousin Jiang Yin'e.

The above facts are confirmed by the report materials, the victim's statement, the testimony of witnesses Zou Weihong, Li Yunsheng, Jiang Yin'e, Jiang Yue'e, and others, as well as photographs of the scene, photographs of the knife used as a tool, and photographs of the victim's injuries. The above evidence, having been examined and verified at trial, can serve as the basis for determining the facts of this case.

The Zhendong District People's Court of Haikou City held:

Article 13 of the Criminal Law provides: "All acts that endanger national sovereignty, territorial integrity and security, split the state, subvert the people's democratic dictatorship and overthrow the socialist system, undermine social and economic order, infringe upon state-owned property or property collectively owned by the working masses, infringe upon citizens' private property, infringe upon citizens' personal rights, democratic rights and other rights, and other acts that endanger society, are crimes if they are punishable according to law. However, if the circumstances are clearly minor and the harm is not serious, they are not considered crimes." The right to bodily freedom and the right to health are important components of a citizen's personality rights. The defendant Huang Yongzhu, together with Chen Bo and others carrying weapons, seized and controlled Zou Hongxing. When their plot was exposed, this group slashed Zou Hongxing, causing minor injuries, seriously infringing upon Zou Hongxing's personal rights, and should be punished according to law. There is no dispute that the acts of Huang Yongzhu and others constituted a joint crime. Since the co-defendants are all at large, and there is no evidence to prove that it was Huang Yongzhu who slashed Zou Hongxing, Huang Yongzhu should not bear responsibility for that act; there is also no dispute on this point. The focus of the dispute between the prosecution and the defense is whether Huang Yongzhu's conduct constitutes the crime of kidnapping under Article 239, paragraph 1 of the Criminal Law or the crime of illegal detention under Article 238, paragraph 3.

Article 239, paragraph 1 of the Criminal Law provides: "Whoever kidnaps another person for the purpose of extorting property, or kidnaps another person as a hostage, shall be sentenced to fixed-term imprisonment of not less than ten years or life imprisonment, and shall also be fined or have his property confiscated; if the kidnapped person is killed or dies as a result of the kidnapping, the offender shall be sentenced to death and shall also have his property confiscated."

The crime of kidnapping provided for in this Article refers to the act of seizing another person by means of violence, coercion, anesthesia, or other methods for the purpose of extorting property or obtaining a hostage. The subject of this crime is a natural person who has reached the age of criminal responsibility and has the capacity for criminal responsibility. The object infringed upon is the victim's right to life, right to health, and right to personal freedom, and the target of the infringement is any living natural person. The objective aspect of the crime is the act of, against the victim's will, by means of violence, coercion, or other methods, moving the victim from his or her original location and controlling him or her when the victim is unable, dares not, or is unaware of the possibility of resistance. The subjective aspect of the crime is direct intent, with the purpose of extorting property or taking the victim as a hostage.

Article 238 of the Criminal Law provides: "Whoever unlawfully detains another person or otherwise unlawfully deprives another person of his personal freedom shall be sentenced to fixed-term imprisonment of not more than three years, criminal detention, public surveillance, or deprivation of political rights. If there are circumstances of beating or humiliation, the offender shall be given a heavier punishment." "Whoever commits the crime mentioned in the preceding paragraph and causes serious injury to another person shall be sentenced to fixed-term imprisonment of not less than three years but not more than ten years; if death is caused, the offender shall be sentenced to fixed-term imprisonment of not less than ten years. If violence is used to cause injury or death, the offender shall be convicted and punished according to the provisions of Articles 234 and 232 of this Law." "Whoever unlawfully detains or seizes another person for the purpose of recovering a debt shall be punished according to the provisions of the preceding two paragraphs." "If a state functionary, by taking advantage of his office, commits any of the crimes mentioned in the preceding three paragraphs, he shall be given a heavier punishment according to the provisions of the preceding three paragraphs."

The crime of illegal detention provided for in this Article refers to the act of unlawfully depriving another person of his personal freedom by means of detention, confinement, or other coercive methods. The subject of this crime is often a state functionary, but may also be an ordinary citizen who has reached the age of criminal responsibility and has the capacity for criminal responsibility. The object infringed upon is the victim's right to bodily freedom, i.e., the right of a citizen to act or refrain from acting within the scope provided by law, according to his own will and interests. The target of the infringement is any natural person who enjoys personal rights according to law. The objective aspect of the crime is the act of unlawfully detaining, arresting, imprisoning, or otherwise depriving another person of his personal freedom without legal basis or without following legal procedures. The subjective aspect of the crime is direct intent, with the purpose of depriving another person of his personal freedom. According to paragraph 3 of this Article, the act of unlawfully depriving a debtor or his relatives of personal freedom for the purpose of recovering a debt constitutes the crime of illegal detention.

From the above analysis, it can be seen that the crime of kidnapping for the purpose of extorting property and the crime of illegal detention for the purpose of recovering a debt have many similarities. The subjects of both crimes can be ordinary citizens. The objects infringed upon by both crimes include the right to personal freedom. The objective aspects of both crimes involve acts of depriving another person of his personal freedom by coercive means. The subjective aspects of both crimes aim to obtain property. The difference between the two crimes lies in: In the crime of kidnapping aimed at obtaining property, the property extorted belongs to others, usually the victim or his relatives; before committing the crime, the offender generally has no property exchange relationship with the victim or his relatives. The debt demanded in the crime of illegal detention is a debt owed by the victim or his relatives to the offender; before committing the crime, the offender has a creditor-debtor relationship with the victim or his relatives.

In this case, the defendant Huang Yongzhu, deceived by the propaganda of his upliner Jiang Yue'e, who was a relative of the victim Zou Hongxing, paid RMB 3,900 to Jiang Yue'e to participate in pyramid scheme activities. During the pyramid scheme training, fellow trainees Huang Jian, Wang Fei, Chen Bo, and others saw through the pyramid scheme fraud and encouraged the trainees to go to their upliner to get their money back. Encouraged by these people, Huang Yongzhu participated in the act of seizing Zou Hongxing. Jiang Yue'e owed Huang Yongzhu only RMB 3,900, but Huang Yongzhu and his group demanded RMB 60,000 by seizing Zou Hongxing. Was this extortion of property? The answer is no. Because: 1. Although Jiang Yue'e owed Huang Yongzhu only RMB 3,900, and Huang Yongzhu consistently stated in his confessions regarding the purpose of seizing Zou Hongxing that he only wanted to get back his own RMB 3,900 investment, "We couldn't find Jiang Yue'e, so we seized Zou Hongxing and forced Zou Hongxing's wife to return the money we paid for the pyramid scheme." This is consistent with Zou Hongxing's statement: "They wanted to find Jiang Yue'e to get back their RMB 3,900 for the pyramid scheme, but couldn't find Jiang Yue'e, and since I have a family relationship with Jiang Yue'e, they came after me." This shows that recovering a debt was the sole purpose of Huang Yongzhu's participation in seizing Zou Hongxing. 2. In explaining why his accomplices participated in seizing Zou Hongxing, Huang Yongzhu stated that except for himself, who had not developed any downline, the other accomplices all had downlines; these accomplices not only wanted to recover their own RMB 3,900, but also wanted to recover RMB 3,900 for their downline members. When asked about the facts of this case, pyramid scheme participant Liu Ronghu also stated: "Later I heard that they (referring to the group that seized Zou Hongxing) went to Haijing Garden again and controlled the intermediary, not allowing the intermediary to escape, so that they could get our money refunded to us," and said that Wang Fei, who participated in seizing Zou Hongxing, was the upliner of his upliner. Liu Ronghu's statement corroborates the truth of Huang Yongzhu's above confession. 3. A total of eight persons participated in seizing Zou Hongxing at various times, seven of whom were downline members developed by Jiang Yue'e. Based on each of these seven persons paying RMB 3,900 to Jiang Yue'e, the total amount is RMB 27,300. Considering that some may also have been demanding the return of their downline members' investments, a total debt demand of RMB 60,000 is understandable. 4. This group of people who participated in seizing Zou Hongxing were deceived by Jiang Yue'e and others into coming to Hainan to engage in pyramid scheme activities. In addition to each paying an investment of RMB 3,900, they also spent an average of several thousand yuan on travel expenses and living expenses during the several months of so-called training. In their view, these losses were caused by Jiang Yue'e and should be repaid by her. Therefore, each of them intended to demand far more than just RMB 3,900 from Jiang Yue'e. As the victim Zou Hongxing stated, "Jiang Yue'e collected RMB 3,900 from each of them, and they spent several thousand yuan during this period doing the pyramid scheme, so each of them wanted to get back RMB 10,000." These circumstances indicate that although the group that participated in seizing Zou Hongxing demanded RMB 60,000, there was a reason for it, and the purpose was still to recover a debt, without any extortion element.

The defendant Huang Yongzhu and others seized the victim Zou Hongxing in order to recover their pyramid scheme investment payments. Pyramid schemes are illegal, and the creditor-debtor rights arising from participating in illegal activities are also illegal and not protected by law. However, the illegality of the debt does not negate the fact that the purpose of seizing Zou Hongxing was to recover a debt. The Supreme People's Court, in its "Interpretation on the Issue of How to Convict the Act of Unlawfully Detaining Another Person for the Purpose of Recovering a Debt Not Protected by Law" (Fa Shi [2000] No. 19), provides that if an actor unlawfully detains or seizes another person for the purpose of recovering a debt not protected by law, such as a usurious loan or a gambling debt, the actor shall be convicted and punished according to the crime of illegal detention under Article 238 of the Criminal Law. Thus, the existence of a debt is an important boundary for distinguishing the crime of kidnapping from the crime of illegal detention, and whether the debt is lawful is not a boundary for distinguishing the two crimes. As long as the actor, for the purpose of recovering a debt, uses coercive means to unlawfully deprive another person of his personal freedom, even if the debt sought to be recovered is illegal, the act should be punished as the crime of illegal detention. The opinion of Huang Yongzhu's defense counsel that Huang Yongzhu's conduct constitutes the crime of illegal detention should be adopted.

The indictment alleged that the defendant Huang Yongzhu, acting in concert with Chen Bo, Huang Jian, Wang Fei, Su Rong, Zhang Jun, Tang Bo, Jiang Bo, and others carrying weapons, seized and controlled Zou Hongxing, who was engaged in illegal pyramid scheme activities, thereby depriving Zou Hongxing of his right to bodily freedom, and by this means demanded RMB 60,000 from Zou Hongxing's wife. When their plot was exposed, someone from this group took advantage of the chaos to slash Zou Hongxing, causing minor injuries. The facts are clear and the evidence is sufficient. The indictment alleged that Huang Yongzhu committed the crime of kidnapping, but the trial results can only determine that Huang Yongzhu's conduct constitutes the crime of illegal detention. When the facts that can be determined after trial support a different crime from that alleged in the indictment, can the people's court directly render a judgment? Does this violate the statutory procedures of criminal proceedings? The Supreme People's Court, in its "Interpretation on Several Issues Concerning the Implementation of the Criminal Procedure Law of the PRC" (Fa Shi [1998] No. 23), Article 176(2), clearly explains: "If the facts alleged in the indictment are clear and the evidence is reliable and sufficient, but the crime alleged in the indictment is inconsistent with the crime determined by the people's court after trial, a guilty verdict shall be rendered." According to this provision, the people's court has the authority to change the crime charged by the prosecutorial authority.

The criminal circumstances of the defendant Huang Yongzhu and his group were vile and the impact was relatively harmful, and they should be severely punished according to law. Huang Yongzhu's defense counsel submitted that Huang Yongzhu was an accomplice in this case and should be given a lighter punishment. Since all co-defendants in this case are at large, there is insufficient evidence to determine whether he was an accomplice based on the facts of this case and Huang Yongzhu's role and position in the joint crime, so this defense argument is not adopted. Given that there were certain social reasons for the occurrence of this case, that Huang Yongzhu was a first-time offender, and that his attitude of confession was relatively good, a lighter punishment may be imposed on a discretionary basis. Accordingly, the Zhendong District People's Court of Haikou City rendered the following judgment on September 18, 2000:

The defendant Huang Yongzhu is convicted of the crime of illegal detention and sentenced to two years' imprisonment.

After the judgment of first instance, the Zhendong District People's Procuratorate of Haikou City filed a protest with the Haikou Intermediate People's Court of Hainan Province on the grounds that the defendant Huang Yongzhu's conduct should have been classified as the crime of kidnapping and that the application of law in the first-instance judgment was improper. During the second-instance proceedings, the procuratorate applied to withdraw the protest. The Haikou Intermediate People's Court, upon review, held that the request of the Zhendong District People's Procuratorate of Haikou City to withdraw the protest complied with legal provisions, and accordingly, on November 24, 2000, in accordance with Article 241 of the "Interpretation on Several Issues Concerning the Implementation of the Criminal Procedure Law of the PRC," ruled:

Permission is granted for the Zhendong District People's Procuratorate of Haikou City to withdraw its protest.
